source.text: The lowest of the slices' hottest cells: the end slice (index 0), which makes the least heat. Slice 0 of 9 (centre at 0.0212 m, heat rate 5.455 kW/m, coolant 573 K): the closed-form series solution of that slice gives 773.5523 K at the centre. The power shape is a cosine, normalised to an average of 1 (the slice at the middle has (pi/2) cos(0) = 1.571 of the average). The solver's slices exchange a little heat along the height, which this solution does not have, so the tolerance is the sum of: the mesh bound 5 x 144.71 K / 100^2 = 0.072 K; the axial conduction allowance 3 x 0.00099 (the estimate as a fraction of the largest rise) x 1154.9 K (the largest rise of any slice above its coolant) = 3.415 K; the cosine's 41-point table, 1e-3 of the slice's rise of 200.6 K = 0.201 K; rounded up to 0.05 K (3.7 K), fixed before any run.
source.check: Second method: FEED's own per-slice closed form (src/core/closedForm.ts through axialSummary, tests/seedOracleStack.test.ts, to 1e-3 K apart from the cosine's table term), and the real solver (FEED_SOLVER=1): every check of the run passes and the solver's slice peaks are inside the tolerances.

coverage.domain: synthetic pin (constant conductivities, convective boundary 573 K and 30000 W/m2/K on every slice) as 9 radial slices over 0.381 m with a cosine power shape, 20 kW/m on average (31.4 kW/m at the peak)
